title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Split Peak: Dow Rides, Tech Paddles in Place
conditions.summary: The Dow and small caps rallied as money rotated into health care and other defensive groups, while the Nasdaq finished flat. Oil eased and the 10-year yield dipped but held above 5.1%.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: Money rotated from tech into health care, utilities, staples and REITs; health care hit an all-time high led by Eli Lilly (about +5%).
An early tech bounce faded as AI spending, debt worries and 5%-plus yields weighed; the S&P ranged from 7,668 to 7,748.
Best sectors: health care, utilities, consumer staples, real estate. Laggard: technology.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: September housing starts were 1.221 million, below the 1.305 million expected; permits were 1.400 million, slightly above forecasts.
September pending home sales fell 7.3% versus no change expected, pressuring homebuilders and real estate.
The 10-year yield slipped about 2 basis points to 5.12%; the dollar index fell 0.27% to 101.70.
WTI crude fell 1.8% to about $101.79 on hopes for Middle East diplomacy; gold eased 0.4% to $4,142.60.
The Fed is in its pre-meeting blackout; traders expect rates to hold at next week's meeting.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: LLY (Eli Lilly): about +5% — metabolic drug pipeline progress; hit a 52-week high.
MRNA (Moderna): +6.1% — 52-week high ahead of melanoma vaccine data due Oct 24.
MMM (3M): about +4% — earnings beat, higher guidance and a data-center deal with Amazon.
NOC (Northrop Grumman) and RTX: higher — earnings beats and backlog growth.
GM (General Motors): -7.5% — beat estimates and added a $20B buyback, but guidance implies a weaker Q4.
GE (GE Aerospace): -3.8% — fell despite a beat and raised guidance.
META (Meta Platforms): about -2% — fifth straight decline ahead of Wednesday's report.
NFLX (Netflix): -1.7% in the session, then about -5% after hours on soft guidance.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Before the open: GM, GE Aerospace, 3M, RTX, Northrop Grumman, Hasbro, Halliburton and Equifax reported; Hasbro and RTX raised full-year outlooks, Equifax trimmed its guidance midpoint.
After the close: SpaceX beat with revenue up 161% to $14.6B and EPS of $0.35 vs about $0.13 expected, its first profit since the IPO; shares rose about 2% after hours.
After the close: Netflix revenue rose 12% to $12.9B with EPS of $0.87, but a muted Q4 outlook sent shares down about 5% after hours.

sections.title: Business News
items: Salesforce agreed to buy Braze for $47.50 a share in cash, about $5.66 billion in enterprise value.
Qiagen rose on a report that EQT is in advanced talks to acquire it.
DaVita and Fresenius Medical Care fell on reports of a new Trump administration kidney-care plan.
Loop Capital cut Apple to Hold and lowered its target to $330, citing reduced iPhone shipments.
Micron will fund Indium Corp.'s critical-minerals processing expansion in Rome, New York, under a long-term supply deal.

sections.title: On Deck
items: No major U.S. economic reports are scheduled for Wednesday, Oct 21.
Fed officials remain in their blackout period through Oct 29, so no Fed speakers.
Morning earnings include Danaher, Thermo Fisher, Abbott, AT&T and Philip Morris.
Later reports include Tesla, Meta, IBM, Lam Research and Texas Instruments.
Thursday, Oct 22: up to 1.3 billion SpaceX shares become freely tradable as a lockup ends.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, October twentieth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down over the water, and the last set of the day just rolled through. Gus the wonder dog spent the whole afternoon guarding the cooler like a lifeguard on duty. Say good evening to the crew, Gus! Here's the final set. It was a split lineup. The Dow rallied about five hundred thirty points, or one percent, to roughly fifty-two thousand five hundred. The S and P five hundred added about three tenths of a percent to seven thousand seven hundred twelve. The Nasdaq finished flat after an early tech bounce faded. Small caps starred, with the Russell two thousand up more than one and a half percent. Money rotated out of tech and into health care, utilities and staples. Health care hit an all-time high, led by Eli Lilly, up about five percent on drug pipeline progress. Eli Lilly rode that one all the way to the sand. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Wind and weather. Crude fell almost two percent to about one hundred one dollars on hopes for Middle East diplomacy. The ten year Treasury yield slipped two basis points to about five point one two percent. Housing data was soft. September housing starts missed forecasts, and pending home sales plunged seven percent. The Fed is in its quiet period before next week's meeting, and traders expect a hold. Now the lineup. General Motors wiped out, down about seven and a half percent, as its outlook pointed to a weaker fourth quarter. GE Aerospace fell almost four percent despite a beat. Three M climbed about four percent on a beat and an Amazon data center deal. Moderna jumped six percent to a fifty two week high. Meta slid for a fifth straight day before tomorrow's report. Gnarly stuff in big tech. On the tide chart, SpaceX posted its first profit since going public, with revenue up one hundred sixty one percent. It rose about two percent after hours. Netflix beat on profit but gave a soft outlook, and fell about five percent after hours. Beach talk. Salesforce agreed to buy Braze for about five point seven billion dollars. Qiagen rose on a report of buyout talks. Loop Capital cut Apple to hold. And in Seoul, a grommet called Elice sank more than thirty percent on its first day. Tough first wave, little grom. Tomorrow's forecast. No major economic reports, and no Fed speakers. In the morning, Danaher, Thermo Fisher, Abbott and A T and T report. Later, Tesla, Meta and I B M are on deck. So wax the board tonight. Want a read on a stock, E T F or futures contract? Type it into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. Catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning. Remember, the soul surfer rides for the long haul, not the hype. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
